title: Sales Architects Pocket Guide: Inference Positioning, Pricing Rationale, Competitive Angles, and Security FAQ
author: Marisol Vega
summary: A compact, field-ready guide for sales architects and SEs to position Redwood Inference for pilots and deals. Includes persona-aligned messaging, competitive battlecards, pragmatic pricing scenarios, a demo/pitch checklist, and a short security FAQ to close technical questions during trials.
body:
Overview:
This pocket guide is built for customer-facing engineers and sales architects who must quickly frame Redwood Inference vs. alternatives, construct pilot economics, and neutralize technical/security objections. Use the one-page sections during calls, and the appendices for follow-up collateral.

Who this is for:
- Sales engineers running technical discovery and pilots
- Solution architects designing reference integration patterns
- AEs and CSMs preparing executive summaries and TCO for prospects

Core positioning pillars (one-liners):
1) Production-first inference: predictable latency and cost controls that make LLMs safe to operate at scale.
2) Unified deployment surface: same API + tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private modes for easy pilot -> prod migration.
3) Cost & performance levers: measurable batching, caching, and quantization steps that reduce per-token costs while preserving output quality.

Buyer personas and tailored messages:
- Platform Engineer (SRE/Infra): "We provide a single runtime you can rationalize across teams — predictable latency SLOs, clear autoscaling behavior, and pluggable KMS/HSM for compliance."
- ML/Model Owner: "Ship model changes with versioned rollouts, canary policies, and guards to prevent regressions; built-in eval hooks tie regressions to prompt sets."
- Product/PM: "Turn prototypes into reliable features quickly — same API in hosted and private modes, integrated observability for user-level cost attribution."
- Security/Compliance: "Private deployment options, VPC peering, audit logs, and integrations with enterprise KMS and SIEM reduce risk of data leakage and simplify audits."

Competitive battlecard (quick-read table):
Competitor | Typical claim | Redwood counterpoint | Win when
Major cloud managed endpoints | "We already host your data, one vendor" | Redwood: choose cost/control tradeoffs — dedicated/private for isolation; transparent perf profiles and cost levers | Customer needs predictable cost per token + routing control
Open-source self-host | "Full control, lower licensing" | Redwood: removes ops burden and brittle performance variability; intelligent batching, kernel selection, and fallbacks reduce TCO vs naive self-host stacks | Customer lacks deep infra investment or needs SLOs
Low-cost inference startups | "Cheaper per-token" | Redwood: lower end-to-end cost after caching/batching + better tail latency and enterprise controls; committed plans for predictable throughput | Customer values SLA and enterprise features
Legacy model-hosting vendors | "We do enterprise integrations" | Redwood: modern inference features (KV caching, streaming, function calling) + rollout tooling and clear benchmarks for production apps | Customer migrating from ad-hoc APIs to production-grade inference

How to run a pilot (recommended 6-week plan):
1) Week 0: Discovery & success metrics. Agree on 2–3 SLOs (p50/p95 latency, accuracy/metric on prompt set, cost per 1k requests).
2) Week 1: Environment setup. Host vs private decision; provide API key/access model; deploy onboarding example app.
3) Week 2–3: Integration & test. Wire SDKs, implement streaming paths, enable tracing hooks, run baseline evals.
4) Week 4: Optimization window. Apply batching, enable prefix/KV caching, select quantization profile; run comparative latency & cost tests.
5) Week 5: Business metrics validation. Show end-to-end numbers: cost per 100k tokens, latency percentiles, error rates.
6) Week 6: Executive review & next-step plan. Present rollout plan, committed capacity options, and commercial proposal.

Pricing guidance (simple scenarios and talking points):
- Pricing levers we sell: hosted per-token usage, dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit), and private (license/support + infra).
- Early pilot pricing recommendation: offer 1 month of continued low-cost hosted usage (discounted) + fixed 2-week optimization window with a solutions engineer.

Example TCO scenarios (back-of-envelope):
- Small pilot (100K tokens/day): Hosted at $0.20 per 1K tokens => ~$6/day; optimization expected to reduce token usage by 20% => $4.8/day post-optimizations.
- Production feature (10M tokens/day): If moved to dedicated with reserved GPUs, unit cost often falls 3–6x depending on batching & quantization. Example: Hosted cost $2,000/day vs Dedicated amortized cost $400–700/day after autoscaling and caching optimizations.
Notes for commercial conversations:
- Emphasize predictable committed pricing and burst options for Dedicated deals.
- For enterprises, present blended model: private control plane + hosted fallback to keep costs predictable during spikes.

Pitch/deck recommended flow (6–8 slides):
1) Problem and customer impact (latency, cost, reliability)
2) Redwood value prop: unified inference with production controls
3) How it works at a high level: serving runtime, caching, routing, deployment modes
4) Demo or short video: <30s of API call + latency table
5) Pilot plan & success metrics (use pilot timeline above)
6) Pricing options & simple TCO examples
7) Security and compliance summary (private + KMS + audit logs)
8) Ask: pilot kickoff / POC next steps

Demo & meeting checklist (for SEs):
- Pre-call: collect sample prompt set and expected request profile (QPS, payload size, acceptable latency).
- Bring: sample dashboard screenshot with latency & per-route cost, a prebuilt evaluation script, and a small canary model variant.
- Run: 3-minute live demo showing streaming + function calling or a side-by-side latency/cost chart.
- Post-call: send concise results and the pilot contract template.

Objection handling (short scripts):
- "We can self-host cheaper": "Self-hosting can look cheaper on paper but typically fails to deliver consistent p95 latency and operational overhead — our benchmarks and runbooks convert that unknown into predictable economics."
- "We need on-prem": "We offer private deployment with a customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem package; we’ll map network and KMS requirements during the onboarding session."
- "We're worried about data leakage": "We support VPC peering, per-tenant encryption keys, audit logs, and an option to disable external model telemetry. We can walk your security team through a checklist and run a whitebox pen test as part of the enterprise package."

Short security FAQ for prospects (field-ready answers):
Q: Where is customer data stored?
A: For hosted customers data resides in the chosen cloud region; for Dedicated customers we provide isolated GPU pools and for Private customers data stays in the customer VPC/on-prem environment.

Q: Do you integrate with KMS/HSM?
A: Yes. We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault and can integrate with customer HSMs for private deployments; keys can be customer-managed.

Q: Can we run in an air-gapped environment?
A: Yes. We provide an on-prem package with a private control plane option that supports air-gapped installs for regulated workloads.

Q: What compliance certs or audits do you provide?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II reports; we provide audit artifacts for customers under NDA. For regulated customers we offer additional evidence packages and assist in third-party assessments.

Q: How do you handle telemetry and model usage data?
A: Telemetry and usage are opt-in for hosted environments; Private deployments can disable outbound telemetry. We support log forwarding to customer SIEMs and provide configurable retention windows.

Appendix A — Full technical checklist for security review:
- Network: VPC peering, IP allowlists, dedicated subnets, private DNS
- Identity: SAML/SSO, SCIM, role-based access controls for API keys
- Data protection: Customer-managed keys, TLS everywhere, encryption at rest and in transit
- Observability: Structured audit logs, retention policy options, audit export to S3/SIEM
- Testing: Regular vulnerability scans, annual pen test on enterprise contracts, optional purple-team engagement
